title: project-name: a stage-by-stage migration, one settled plan and one goal per stage

goals.title: The direction is settled: the language split, the target shape, and the migration order
goals.notes: A migration plan starts with a settled decision row, so the later stages do not re-argue the direction. The notes keep the decision and its reasons; later rows cite it instead of restating it.

goals.title: The first stage: the core that everything else rides on, judged byte-for-byte against the original
goals.notes: Stage one of a migration is the kernel the later stages depend on, and its judge is the strongest available: the new implementation must agree with the old one on the same corpus. This row stays active until every member of the family is cross-checked.

goals.title: The second stage: the surface that routes each operation to the new core or back to the old
goals.notes: The after edge keeps the order honest: the surface cannot route to a kernel that is not cross-checked yet. Its own judge will drive one operation through both routes and compare the answers.

goals.title: The last stage: the thin shell that replaces the old host integration
goals.notes: The shell is last in the chain on purpose: it flips the integration over only after the routed surface works. A stage that is not ready stays open and says what is missing.
